subject: incorrect legend for alpha when using geom_line

messages.author: 936ef8c6d12fc338
messages.subject: incorrect legend for alpha when using geom_line
parts:
Dear all,

When I use geom_point() then I get a proper legend for alpha. But not when I use geom_line().

Best regards,

Thierry

library(ggplot2)
n <- 200
dataset <- data.frame(x = rnorm(n), y = rnorm(n), z = runif(n), a = sample(factor(c("A", "B")), n, replace = TRUE))
ggplot(dataset, aes(x = x, y = y, alpha = z, colour = a)) + geom_point()
ggplot(dataset, aes(x = x, y = y, alpha = z, colour = a)) + geom_line()

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: incorrect legend for alpha when using geom_line
parts:
Hi Thierry:

It makes sense to me to map alpha to a continuous variable when
plotting points, but when plotting lines, wouldn't you want all the
points on the same line to have the same alpha transparency? That, to
me, would impel the variable mapped to alpha to be discrete. Out of
curiosity, what's the reason for plotting lines with alpha mapped to a
numeric variable?

Dennis

messages.author: 936ef8c6d12fc338
messages.subject: RE: incorrect legend for alpha when using geom_line
parts:
Hi Dennis,

My coworker insists on make a plot like the one below.

library(ggplot2)
dataset <- expand.grid(X = seq(-10, 10), Y = factor(c("A", "B", "C")), Z = factor(1:2))
dataset$A <- with(dataset, 0.5 - abs(0.5 - pnorm(X, mean = rnorm(3)[Y] + rnorm(2, sd = 3)[Z], sd = 4)))
ggplot(dataset, aes(x = X, y = interaction(Z, Y), colour = Z, alpha = A)) + geom_line(size = 3)

I'd rather go for something like

ggplot(dataset, aes(x = X, y = A, colour = Z, linetype = Y)) + geom_line()

Best regards,

Thierry
